en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its perfectly symmetrical cone shape formed by repeated volcanic eruptions.
The Cagayan River in Northern Luzon is the longest and widest river in the Philippine archipelago.
The critically endangered Philippine eagle, found in Mindanao, is one of the largest and most powerful eagles worldwide.
Laguna de Bay in Luzon is the largest lake in the Philippines and a vital source of freshwater fish.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest peak in the Philippines, standing at approximately 2,954 meters above sea level.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site protecting diverse coral ecosystems.
The amihan is the cool northeast monsoon that brings dry weather to the Philippines between November and February.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao were carved into the mountains by indigenous people over two thousand years ago.
Palawan is the longest island province in the Philippines, known for its extensive limestone karst landscapes and caves.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features an eight-kilometer underground river that flows directly into the sea.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
Taal Volcano in Batangas features a main crater lake situated on Volcano Island within the larger Lake Taal.
